title: Outline on Label3D can draw over blended text pixels when using AlphaCut=Opaque Pre-Pass
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in v4.6.1 ### System information Godot v4.6.1.mrlink3.mono (5ffa4f096) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900K (32 threads) - 127.7 GiB memory ### Issue description I am using Opaque Pre-Pass for my Label3D text but found it looks wrong when there is an outline. Here is what it looks like out of the box: The issue appears to be that the outline's opaque pixels may be drawn after the text's alpha-blended pixels and stomp over them. When I apply the following change to label_3d.cpp's _generate_glyph_surfaces (I have no idea if this is a work-around or a proper fix!) to always set a render priority, then the text renders correctly: ```diff - if (get_alpha_cut_mode() == ALPHA_CUT_DISABLED) { RS::get_singleton()->material_set_render_priority(surf.material, p_priority); - } else { + if (get_alpha_cut_mode() != ALPHA_CUT_DISABLED) { surf.z_shift = p_priority * pixel_size; } ``` This sets render priority for all modes, but in reality I think render priority might only need to be set for ALPHA_CUT_DISABLED and ALPHA_CUT_OPAQUE_PREPASS because the other two modes only write opaque pixels. I am using this with OpenXR (the depth is important for reprojection quality and depth testing with composition layers). Here's another comparison (top=no fix, bottom=fixed) of small text at a distance. This case uses MSDF font, but issue is same whether MSDF or not: ### Steps to reproduce Create a Label3D Change AlphaCut to Opaque Pre-pass Result: Sometimes it looks correct/wrong depending on perspective (sorting order?), and sometimes it just always looks wrong. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [label3d_opaqueprepass.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25727862/label3d_opaqueprepass.zip)
